cause: The `add_item` endpoint assumes `request.get_json()` always returns a dictionary or `None`, but valid JSON request bodies can also be a top-level array. When a client sends a non-empty JSON list, `request.get_json(silent=True) or {}` evaluates to the `list`, causing an `AttributeError` when attempting to call `.get("name")`.

The `add_item` endpoint assumes `request.get_json(silent=True)` always returns a dictionary, but valid JSON payloads can also be lists or other primitives. When a client submits a non-empty JSON array, `data` is a `list`, which does not have a `.get()` method, raising an `AttributeError`.
